2609.20139.title: Cross-Modal Attention Acts as a Frequency Filter: Why Verbose Prompts Improve Robustness in Vision-Language Models
2609.20139.paper_summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) are fragile under image corruption. We find that the wording of the question affects VLMs in two opposite ways. Verbose questions make VLMs substantially more robust---e.g., rephrasing "Is there a cat?" into "Please look carefully and answer: is there a cat?". Conversely, VLMs become more fragile under corruption when the question is semantically complex or finer-grained, e.g., "what colour is the cup left of the chair?" instead of "is there a cup?". Both effects stem from question-conditioned cross-modal attention, which induces a spectral filter over image patches: verbose questions broaden its frequency support, while fine-grained questions concentrate it onto fewer visual scales. The model's answer drifts most when this filter and the corruption sit on the same spatial frequencies. We test the filter view on Qwen3-VL and LLaVA-OneVision across GQA and CLEVR; verbose paraphrasing reduces drift variance by 70--81% on the 8B models. The practical recipe---pad the prompt---further yields measurable gains in accuracy, even under image corruption.
2609.20139.paper_summary_zh: 視覺語言模型（VLMs）在影像損壞下非常脆弱。<lb/>我們發現問題的措辭以兩種相反的方式影響VLMs。<lb/>冗長的問題使VLMs顯著更具魯棒性——例如，將「有貓嗎？」改寫為「請仔細查看並回答：有貓嗎？」。<lb/>相反，當問題在語義上複雜或更細緻時，VLMs在損壞下變得更脆弱，例如，「椅子左邊的杯子是什麼顏色？」而不是「有杯子嗎？」。<lb/>這兩種效應源於基於問題的跨模態注意力，該注意力對影像區塊產生了一種頻譜濾波器：冗長的問題擴大了其頻率支持，而細緻的問題則將其集中在較少的視覺尺度上。<lb/>當這個濾波器和損壞位於相同的空間頻率時，模型的答案漂移最為明顯。<lb/>我們在GQA和CLEVR上對Qwen3-VL和LLaVA-OneVision測試了濾波器視角；冗長的改寫使8B模型的漂移方差減少了70--81%。<lb/>這個實用的配方——填充提示——在影像損壞下進一步帶來可測量的準確性提升。
